Joining the midpoints of a square creates a new square with half the area of the original. Since the small square has area 6 cm², the medium square has area 2 × 6 = 12 cm². From the image, identify that each inner square is rotated 45 degrees relative to the square that contains it, with its vertices at the containing square's side midpoints. From the text, take the small square area as 6 cm^2. Let the medium square have side length m. Since a square with diagonal d has area d^2/2, the small square area is m^2/2 = 6, so the medium square area m^2 = 12. Now let the large square have side length L.
